step.text: A spreadsheet from your system, listing every account's items and what it pays, is usually all we need.

@graph.name: Do I need a TrueCommerce alternative to get restaurants ordering digitally?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. TrueCommerce still looks after chains, suppliers and your Shop storefront if you run one. We give phone-ordering restaurants their own way in: their chef reads the order aloud into our app, checks it and sends, and your EDI is left as it is.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than TrueCommerce?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one job: moving a restaurant from phone calls onto an app, where its chef speaks each order and checks it before sending. Connecting chains, onboarding suppliers and running a storefront are TrueCommerce's work, so we are not a TrueCommerce alternative and do not try to be.

@graph.name: What does a restaurant have to set up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only the app: no mapping and no document testing on its side. We open its account from the items you already sell it, and we will show you in a demo how a chef gets started. A restaurant group that already sends you EDI can keep sending it through TrueCommerce.

@graph.name: What about TrueCommerce Shop for online ordering?

acceptedAnswer.text: Shop gives customers an always-open portal where they can reorder, use quick order and see their own pricing. It is made for the people happy to browse a website. Our app is for the chefs who never took it up and still call: they say what they need aloud rather than search a catalog. Whatever the chef sends in our app skips Shop, so Shop's order history will not include it; it comes to you by email, EDI or the API instead.

@graph.name: Does it link to TrueCommerce, and will we still type up restaurant orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. TrueCommerce and VoiceOrder Solutions are separate businesses with no connection built between the products, and each supports only its own product. An order from our app that goes as EDI or through our API can load with nobody keying it, if your ERP is set up to take it; the demo is where we check. Over email, someone at your end still enters it, but there is no call to answer, write up or read back: they key it from the chef's own reviewed order. TrueCommerce also offers a connector for emailed and faxed orders; nothing on our side was built for it, and we do not promise that it reads ours. Customer accounts, stock counts and invoices stay in your ERP; we hold the guides, the prices in them, and the orders each chef sends from the app. A call to you still gets no number from us. The app can still get an item wrong, which is why the chef looks over the list before sending.

@graph.name: We use TrueCommerce with our own suppliers. Does this touch that?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Purchase orders, shipping notices and invoices with your suppliers stay in TrueCommerce and your ERP. We only handle the orders restaurants place with you, and nothing we do reaches your suppliers.

@graph.name: How soon could we start, and how is it quoted?

acceptedAnswer.text: Getting most distributors set up takes 24 to 48 hours, without a single change inside TrueCommerce. You send the usual items for each account, often as an export from your system, and we load them into our admin, then open an account for each restaurant. Its chef then installs the app, and most restaurants have ordered through it by the end of that day. TrueCommerce sets custom pricing for each business by quote, and we quote per distributor as well. A TrueCommerce replacement would move every partner connection to a new provider; bringing in our app leaves each of them where it is.
